target_customer: Surgeons, hospitals and medical device manufacturers (MedTech sales, field service and quality teams) in orthopaedics and trauma surgery
problem: Surgeons cannot easily find reliable answers about implants and procedures because manufacturer documentation, hospital protocols and medical literature are scattered across many sources.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals and to MedTech manufacturers; longer term a sourcing and ordering layer for surgical devices (stated direction, not yet operating)
product_category: Medical device knowledge platform with source-backed AI search

founders.name: Vincent Paffrath
education: ETH Zurich, PhD researcher in generative and agentic AI (degree status not stated)

founders.name: Maximilian Becker
education: ETH Zurich, former AI researcher (degree details not stated)

founders.name: Alexander Schulz
founders.background_notes: Built electronics and embedded software for biomedical instruments.

competitors.name: Johnson & Johnson MedTech Polyphonic
competitors.what: Digital surgical ecosystem with applications for surgical video, telepresence and planning, aspiring to be device agnostic

competitors.name: Stryker SmartHospital Platform
competitors.what: Digital foundation connecting devices, data and care teams across the hospital; focus on connectivity and alerts, not surgical instructions

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval and source-backed AI over heterogeneous manufacturer documents is standard engineering, but ingesting and structuring implant documentation and hospital protocols across manufacturers takes sustained data work.

defensibility.rationale: Structured manufacturer content, hospital SOPs and relationships with chief physicians and manufacturers could compound, but general AI search tools could copy the interface.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large manufacturers launched their own digital platforms (Polyphonic 2024, SmartHospital March 2026) but those do not target cross-manufacturer instruction search; several of them are listed as CONUS customers or partners on its site.

market_need_then: Hospitals handle many implant systems whose instructions sit in separate manufacturer documents; the company reports live use in 27 hospitals and 49 more onboarding, self reported on the YC page.

branding.domain_note: Uses conus-med.com, not the bare .com; date not stated

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and clinical, tagline: Surgery is complex. Finding answers shouldn't be.

brand_strength.rationale: Only company site and a launch blog post found; no press on the brand itself. Name resembles CONMED in search results, which is a confusion risk.

outcome_analysis: CONUS is an active Fall 2026 YC company with early traction reported by the company itself: live in about 27 German and European hospitals and co-founded with five chief physicians in trauma surgery and orthopaedics, which gives clinical access. No funding round, exit or failure has been reported publicly. The main risks are that manufacturers build their own platforms and that general AI tools commoditize search.
notes: Hospital count is inconsistent across the YC page (27 live, more than 20, 25). Founded year not stated. No funding amounts found in two searches; the Dealroom page for CONUS Medical Solutions was paywalled. The fondo.com post is a launch write-up and not independent. No outcome news beyond October 2026 found.
